dedupe_keys.name: snis sistema nacional de informacoes sobre saneamento historical series succeeded by sinisa

description: SNIS, Brazil's National Sanitation Information System, is described by the Ministry of Cities as the largest and most important information system of the Brazilian sanitation sector. Created in 1996 and run by the national sanitation secretariat, it collects data every year from municipalities and service providers on the operational, managerial, financial and quality aspects of water and sewage services (SNIS-AE), urban solid waste (SNIS-RS) and urban stormwater drainage (SNIS-AP), to support public policy, investment, regulation, performance assessment and social control. Coverage is national at municipality and provider level, with annual series from 1995 to 2022; from 2024 collection moved to SINISA, the successor system set by the sanitation law. Results are published as annual Diagnósticos and through the Série Histórica web application; the federal open-data portal lists the series under a Creative Commons Attribution licence, free of charge, and Base dos Dados offers cleaned municipal tables for download and BigQuery. Caveats: data are self-reported by providers and municipalities with varying completeness, indicator definitions changed over time, the cleaned tables hold only a subset of SNIS, and the government portals were partly unreachable from the cataloguing environment. Simulation uses: calibrating demand, coverage, losses and service performance in Brazilian water, sewage and drainage models, and planning investment. Related records: the European UWWTD plant data (data-uwwtd-treatment-plants) and the US Clean Watersheds Needs Survey (data-epa-clean-watersheds-needs-survey-2022) are comparable national sources.
